subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw memory-core preserve Markdown heading boundaries by default, add an explicit strategy/config surface, or leave this to a plugin/MVP redesign?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the permanent fix affects chunking defaults, index identity, upgrade reindexing, and the boundary between bundled memory-core behavior and optional plugin/ClawHub capability.

options.title: Approve narrow heading-aware chunking
options.body: Keep this issue open for a focused memory-core design that preserves section boundaries and explicitly handles reindex/upgrade behavior, while separating entity extraction.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub first
options.body: Treat both heading chunking and extraction as external memory-plugin experiments unless maintainers identify a missing SDK seam.

options.title: Fold into Memory MVP design
options.body: Defer this issue until the broader memory schema, write pipeline, and operator-surface issues settle the default memory lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow heading-aware chunking
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a focused memory-core design that preserves section boundaries and explicitly handles reindex/upgrade behavior, while separating entity extraction.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent history across Memory Wiki, corpus integration, and the entity/synthesis-adjacent surfaces that shape the product boundary.
